faq.q: What are the most common pickleball injuries?
faq.a: Pickleball is quick at the kitchen line and hard on knees, shoulders and feet. Common complaints include knee pain, Achilles issues, shoulder strain, and injuries from falls.

faq.q: When should I get a pickleball injury checked?
faq.a: If pain keeps coming back, stops you moving normally, or has not settled, talk it through with a registered physiotherapist. Get urgent care for severe pain, a joint that looks out of place, numbness, or if you cannot put weight on a leg. In an emergency, call 911.

faq.q: Can a physiotherapist assess a pickleball injury on video?
faq.a: Yes. A Calm Joints video assessment is with a registered physiotherapist. They look at how you move and talk through next steps with you, including whether an in-person visit makes sense. Book a time that fits around your games.
